title: Minimal-polynomial root-product norm identity over a p-adic field
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $K=\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its normalized absolute value [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and $\Omega/K$ an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure] equipped with an absolute value extending that of $K$. Let $H\in K[X]$ be monic of degree $r\geq0$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], with roots $c_1,\ldots,c_r\in\Omega$ counted with multiplicity. For $\alpha\in\Omega$, let $f\in K[T]$ be its minimal polynomial over $K$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and put $m=\deg f\geq1$. Then
$$\left|\prod_{i=1}^r f(c_i)\right|=|H(\alpha)|^m.$$
All evaluations and products are computed in $\Omega$ using the given inclusion of $K$, and the empty product is $1$.

source.place: Chapter I, proof of Lemma 10.21, printed p.51: the displayed identity for the product of F(a_i), with F the minimum polynomial of alpha, and its identical Q formula.

proof.text: The minimal polynomial $f$ is monic by [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Apply [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization] in $\Omega$ to $f$ and $H$. Since their leading coefficients are $1$, write $f(T)=\prod_{j=1}^m(T-\alpha_j)$ and $H(T)=\prod_{i=1}^r(T-c_i)$, listing roots with multiplicity. The numbers of factors are $m$ and $r$ by degrees. In particular $f(\alpha_j)=0$ for every $j$. This includes $H=1$, with no factors.

source.place: Chapter I, proof of Lemma 10.21, printed p.51: factorization by conjugates and the two displayed root-product identities.

proof.text: The extension $\Omega/K$ is algebraic by [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and normal: the minimal polynomial of every element splits in the algebraically closed field $\Omega$, by the factorization lemma of step 1. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-normal-extension-conjugate-by-automorphism], applied to $\alpha$ and each root $\alpha_j$ of $f$, supplies a $K$-automorphism $\sigma_j$ of $\Omega$ with $\sigma_j(\alpha)=\alpha_j$.

source.place: Chapter I, proof of Lemma 10.21, printed p.51: factorization by conjugates and the two displayed root-product identities.

proof.text: The base $K=\mathbf Q_\ell$ is complete, nontrivially valued and nonarchimedean by [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] (nontriviality follows from $|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}\ne1$). For each $j$, $u_j(z)=|\sigma_j(z)|$ is an absolute value on $\Omega$: multiplicativity and the triangle inequality follow by applying $|\cdot|$ to the corresponding identities for the field automorphism, and $u_j(z)=0$ iff $z=0$. It agrees with $|\cdot|_K$ since $\sigma_j$ fixes $K$. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-absolute-value-unique] to $u_j$ and the given absolute value on the algebraic extension $\Omega/K$. Therefore $|\sigma_j(z)|=|z|$ for all $z$. Writing $H(T)=\sum_k h_kT^k$ gives $H(\alpha_j)=\sum_k h_k\sigma_j(\alpha)^k=\sigma_j(\sum_k h_k\alpha^k)=\sigma_j(H(\alpha))$, hence $|H(\alpha_j)|=|H(\alpha)|$.

source.place: Chapter I, proof of Lemma 10.21, printed p.51: factorization by conjugates and the two displayed root-product identities.

proof.text: Rearrange the finite products from step 1 in the commutative field $\Omega$: $$\prod_i f(c_i)=\prod_{i,j}(c_i-\alpha_j)=(-1)^{rm}\prod_j\prod_i(\alpha_j-c_i)=(-1)^{rm}\prod_j H(\alpha_j).$$ Taking absolute values, $|-1|=1$ and multiplicativity give $|\prod_i f(c_i)|=\prod_j|H(\alpha_j)|=|H(\alpha)|^m$ by step 3. No division or cancellation of evaluations is used, so vanishing evaluations cause no exception. When $r=0$, both sides are $1$ because $H=1$.

source.place: Chapter I, proof of Lemma 10.21, printed p.51: factorization by conjugates and the two displayed root-product identities.

proof_origin.note: Expanded the Milne argument with explicit normal-extension conjugacy and uniqueness of the extending absolute value. The finite-product rearrangement proves the identity without a resultant theorem.

Step 1: the minimal polynomial is monic (def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension) and lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization factors f and H with roots listed with multiplicity, so separability is not assumed. Step 2: Ω is algebraic and normal, and lem-weil-pbc-normal-extension-conjugate-by-automorphism gives σ_j with σ_j(α)=α_j. Step 3: Q_ℓ is complete, nonarchimedean and nontrivial (|ℓ|=1/ℓ), and the new leaf gives |σ_j z|=|z|, hence |H(α_j)|=|H(α)|. Step 4: the signed double product ∏_i f(c_i)=(−1)^{rm}∏_j H(α_j) uses no division. Hand checks: r=0, α∈K, H(α)=0 and ℓ=2, α=√2, H=X all agree. The statement is self-contained and has no proof sketch. lean.statement: theorem abs_prod_minpoly_eq_aeval_pow_natDegree (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra ℚ_[ell] Ω] [IsAlgClosure ℚ_[ell] Ω] (v : AbsoluteValue Ω ℝ) (hv : ∀ x : ℚ_[ell], v (algebraMap ℚ_[ell] Ω x) = ‖x‖) (r : ℕ) (H : Polynomial ℚ_[ell]) (hH : H.Monic) (hdeg : H.natDegree = r) (c : Fin r → Ω) (hc : (↑(List.ofFn c) : Multiset Ω) = (H.map (algebraMap ℚ_[ell] Ω)).roots) (alpha : Ω) : v (∏ i : Fin r, aeval (c i) (minpoly ℚ_[ell] alpha)) = v (aeval alpha H) ^ (minpoly ℚ_[ell] alpha).natDegree

reviewed_lean.note: Every clause matches the node: prime ell, ℚ_[ell] with its normalized norm, any IsAlgClosure Ω, an AbsoluteValue v extending ‖·‖ with no extra assumptions, H monic with natDegree r, roots kept with multiplicity as a multiset, minpoly and its natDegree, and the exact equation. lean.statement is verbatim. Edge cases r=0, repeated roots, H(alpha)=0, alpha in the base and ell=2 are covered. Docstrings carry the source place (Milne AV I Lemma 10.21 p.51), the blueprint tag and all four proof steps. No definitions and proof is sorry only. stmt_deps are imported publicly. Node unchanged from live except the new lean record.
